questions.stem: Explain the trade-offs between direct-mapped and set-associative caches.
markingGuide: Direct-mapped caches are simpler and faster.
Direct-mapped caches suffer from higher conflict misses.

questions.explanation: Direct-mapped caches are straightforward but can lead to frequent conflicts when multiple data blocks map to the same line. questions.stem: Discuss how cache pollution can occur with large cache lines.
markingGuide: Cache pollution occurs when unnecessary data is loaded into the cache.
Larger cache lines increase the likelihood of loading unused data.
This can reduce the effective cache capacity for useful data.
questions.explanation: Cache pollution happens when data that is not needed is loaded into the cache, occupying space that could be used for more frequently accessed data. Larger cache lines can exacerbate this issue by bringing in more contiguous data, some of which may not be used, thus reducing the cache's efficiency.
